Title: Some users may see unwanted add-ins appearing automatically across all Outlook clients

User impact: Users may see unwanted add-ins appearing automatically across all Outlook clients.

More info: These add-ins are configured to be available to users by admins but aren’t expected to be automatically installed.

Current status: The fix deployment has completed. We've determined that this fix is viable for all affected users but to see the impact remediated, users will need to run the following command: "Set-App -Identity "<AppId>" -DefaultStateForUser Disabled -OrganizationApp -PrivateCatalog". After running this command all users who previously installed add-ins may need to install them again. We're providing time for affected users to run this command and remediate impact before we consider this resolved.

Scope of impact: Impact may occur for some users that may see unwanted add-ins appearing automatically across all Outlook clients. This section may be updated as the investigation progresses.

- Delays, failures, or incomplete results when searching for content within Exchange Online mailboxes.
- Delays or failures when sending or receiving email messages.
- Authentication-related errors when accessing Exchange Online services.
- Difficulties accessing or performing actions within Exchange administration experiences.
- Intermittent failures affecting mailbox operations and message delivery work

User impact: Users may experience issues when utilizing multiple Microsoft 365 services.

More info: Impact includes, but may not be limited to, the below services and scenarios. We will update this list as our understanding of the issue progresses.

Microsoft 365 Copilot: 
- Users' Copilot prompts that require Microsoft 365 grounding, such as email content, may fail.
 
OneDrive for Business and SharePoint Online:
-Users may be unable to load or refresh portions of OneDrive and SharePoint, including account and storage information, search results, Favorites, Followed and Shared With Me content, recent files, lists, and news.
-Some users may also experience delayed or failed file opening, Office policy-label retrieval, OneDrive synchronization, mobile camera upload, and video playback.
-Users may see partial page failures, missing or stale content, repeated retries, and operation timeouts rather than a complete platform outage.      

Exchange Online:
-Users may be unable to connect to, or experience degraded functionality, such as failures when attempting to use the search function, within Exchange Online. All connection methods are affected.

Microsoft Teams:
-Users may experience issues with calendar functionality and search. Users’ presence may be stale and not update automatically or through manual adjustment. User location adjustment may fail.
-Microsoft Teams Room (MTR) devices and desktop phones display as offline in the Teams admin center.

Microsoft Purview:
-Users may face intermittent authorization failures across solutions in Purview. Purview admins can’t access the portal.
Additionally, in Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance, users may see errors when loading Communication Compliance policies and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies. Communication Compliance policy creation and evaluation may be delayed.

Microsoft Defender XDR:
-Users may experience intermittent authorization failures across solutions in Defender.
 
Microsoft 365 Admin Center:
-Admins may experience issues authenticating into the admin center.
 
Universal Print: 
-Users may be unable to create, upload, or retrieve print jobs.
